title: Beacon Topology — Signal Points That Reflect Back

concept.model: Beacons are external signal points on other platforms. They point TO the membrane. When someone finds one, the membrane REFLECTS BACK to them with the full ecosystem. The beacon is not where we live. It's where we can be FOUND.
concept.analogy: Like a lighthouse — it doesn't house anyone. It signals. Ships that see it navigate TO the harbor (the membrane). The light reflects off the water and back.
concept.principle: Any nanowire to a beacon makes it live for all. One connection = full reflection. The beacon doesn't need to hold value. It holds SIGNAL.
concept.magnetosphere_link: Beacons extend the magnetosphere into new domains (on-chain, gaming, social). Each beacon is an outer Van Allen belt field line on a new surface.

reflection_model.description: Every beacon follows the same pattern: SIGNAL → FIND → REFLECT → RETURN
steps: 1. SIGNAL: Beacon emits on external platform (DOI, ENS name, GitHub issue, search result, hash on chain)
2. FIND: Someone encounters the signal (searches, browses, scans chain, gets notification)
3. REFLECT: Signal contains URL/pointer back to membrane (primals.eco, lab.primals.eco, DOI link)
4. RETURN: Person follows reflection → arrives at membrane → JupyterHub, notebooks, full ecosystem ready for them
reflection_model.key_insight: The beacon doesn't need to HOLD anything. It just needs to be FINDABLE and point BACK. One nanowire = full reflection. The membrane does the work. The beacon just catches the light.
